title: Slano, Croatia for Seniors: Accessibility Guide 2027
metaDescription: Senior travel guide to Slano, Croatia: accessible hotels, bus links to Dubrovnik, flat walks, beaches, healthcare and day trips, with € prices for 2027.
content:
## Is Slano a Good Destination for Seniors?

Slano is a small bay village on the Dubrovnik Riviera, about 40 km northwest of Dubrovnik on the Adriatic Highway (D8). It has a few hundred residents, a compact waterfront, a small harbour and shops within a few minutes' walk. There are no crowds and no cruise-ship traffic. For travellers who tire in the Dubrovnik Old Town heat, this is its main advantage.

The drawback is distance. Hospitals, the airport and most sightseeing are 40 km or more away. Plan transport before booking.

## Getting to Slano Without a Car

### From Dubrovnik Airport
Dubrovnik Airport (DBV) is roughly 55 km from Slano. The simplest option for seniors is a pre-booked private transfer or taxi, typically about €80–100 depending on the season and luggage. The alternative is a bus from the airport to Dubrovnik bus station, then a second coach to Slano. That adds a transfer with luggage and is tiring after a flight.

### Bus from Dubrovnik
- FlixBus runs Dubrovnik–Slano, with fares from about €5.98 and a journey of 40–50 minutes. The first bus leaves Slano around 06:05 and the last around 22:00, but departures per day are few.
- FlixBus states its coaches on this route are wheelchair-accessible with boarding assistance. Wheelchairs and walking aids travel free.
- Libertas Dubrovnik local line 12 also serves Slano. It is slower (about 45–90 minutes depending on the stop) and runs about every three hours.

**Tip:** The FlixBus stop in Slano is on the D8 highway, by the apartments at the roadside, not at the waterfront. Allow 5–10 minutes with luggage to reach the centre, and ask the accommodation if they can pick you up.

## Accessibility on the Ground

### Terrain and Walking
The waterfront promenade is flat and paved, and benches are spaced along the bay. This is the best part of Slano for walkers who use sticks or rollators. Side streets leading uphill from the harbour are steep in places, and some have worn stone steps. Villas on the slopes can involve 30–60 steps from the road, so ask about step counts before booking.

### Accommodation
The Admiral Grand Hotel is the main five-star property in Slano, at Trg Rudera Boškovića 13. It has two pools, a spa, three restaurants, parking and a beach. It is listed as generally suitable for people with reduced mobility, but request a ground-floor or lift-served room and confirm the route to the beach in writing. Smaller options include apartments and guesthouses along the D8 and the bay. Choose one with a ground-floor entry and a walk-in shower. Hotel Osmine in nearby Banja is another hotel option.

### Beaches and Swimming
Beaches around Slano are pebble and rock, with clear water. Pebbles are difficult for unsteady walkers, and water shoes are worth packing. Hotel beach areas are easier to enter than public coves. Heat peaks from late June to August, so many seniors prefer May, June, September or early October, when daytime temperatures are around 20–27°C.

## Healthcare and Pharmacies

Slano has basic local services, including a pharmacy and a small health clinic. For anything serious, the nearest full hospital is Dubrovnik General Hospital, about 45 minutes by road. Carry the EU Global Health Insurance Card (EHIC/GHIC where valid) and travel insurance, and bring a printed medication list with generic drug names. The European emergency number is 112.

## Day Trips Suited to Seniors

| Trip | Distance from Slano | Senior notes |
|---|---|---|
| Trsteno Arboretum | About 12 km | Shaded gardens, gentle paths, some slopes; entry around €10 |
| Ston and Mali Ston | About 14 km | Oyster bars and salt pans, mostly flat; skip the wall climb |
| Dubrovnik Old Town | About 40 km | Steep stairs and crowds; the main street (Stradun) is flat |
| Mljet ferry | Via Prapratno, near Ston | Longer day, needs good stamina |

The Ston walls are among the longest in Europe, but the climb is steep with uneven steps. Seniors with limited mobility are better off eating oysters in Mali Ston and viewing the walls from the road.

Trsteno is the easiest cultural stop. A taxi from Slano costs roughly €25–35 each way, which is cheaper than a guided tour.

## Practical Tips for Seniors

- **Book a taxi in advance.** Taxis are few and not always at the stand. Ask your accommodation to call one the day before.
- **Skip the Dubrovnik Old Town in July and August.** The extra hour on the bus and the heat on marble steps are usually not worth it. Visit in the early morning or in shoulder season instead.
- **Shop early.** Small shops close for a midday break, and supplies are limited in winter.
- **Eat main meals at lunch.** Konobas along the bay serve grilled fish and local dishes, with mains at roughly €12–25.
- **Winter is quiet.** Some restaurants and services close from November to March, so check before arriving.

## Best Time to Visit

May–June and September–October combine warm sea, lower prices and fewer visitors. Hotel rates in July and August can be a large multiple of spring rates. Water is comfortable for swimming from late May.

faq.question: Is Slano wheelchair accessible?
faq.answer: Partly. The seafront promenade is flat and the Admiral Grand Hotel is described as generally suitable for reduced mobility. Side streets are steep and pebble beaches are hard to cross, so confirm step-free access with the accommodation before booking.

faq.question: How do seniors get from Dubrovnik to Slano?
faq.answer: The easiest ways are a pre-booked transfer or taxi (about €70–90 from the city) or a FlixBus coach from about €5.98, taking 40–50 minutes. FlixBus says its coaches on this route are wheelchair-accessible with boarding help.

faq.question: Is Slano better than Dubrovnik for older travellers?
faq.answer: For a quiet, flat and cooler stay, yes. Dubrovnik has more sights and services but also stairs, crowds and high prices in summer, so many seniors stay in Slano and visit Dubrovnik on one or two days.

faq.question: Is there a hospital in Slano?
faq.answer: No. Slano has a small local clinic and a pharmacy, while the nearest full hospital is Dubrovnik General Hospital, about 45 minutes away. Call 112 in an emergency.

faq.question: When is the best time for seniors to visit Slano?
faq.answer: May, June, September and early October are best, with temperatures around 20–27°C and fewer visitors. July and August are hotter and more expensive.

faq.question: Can seniors visit the Ston walls from Slano?
faq.answer: The walls are about 14 km away, but the climb is steep and uneven, so they are not suitable for limited mobility. Mali Ston's oyster restaurants are flat and easy to reach by taxi.

quickAnswer: Slano suits seniors who want a quiet, flat seafront village 40 km north of Dubrovnik. The waterfront promenade is short and level, and the five-star Admiral Grand Hotel is generally suitable for reduced mobility. Buses to Dubrovnik take 40–50 minutes from about €6. Beaches are pebbly and some lanes are steep.
